newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-MIAMI CENTER ISAAC AUSTIN WINS MOST IMPROVED PLAYER AWARD.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-MIAMI CENTER ISAAC AUSTIN WINS MOST IMPROVED PLAYER AWARD.

text.p: Miami Heat backup centre Isaac Austin capped his return from Turkish exile Saturday by being named winner of the 1996-97 NBA Most Improved Player Award.
Austin, who played for Tuborg Izmir in Turkey last season, was runaway winner in voting by a panel of sports writers and broadcasters, picking up 41 of a possible 115 votes.

Toronto Raptors swingman Doug Christie finished second with 17 votes and Portland Trail Blazers forward Rasheed Wallace was third in the balloting with 13 votes. Fifteen players received Most Improved votes, the NBA said.
The 6-10 (2.08 m) Austin averaged 9.7 points, 5.8 rebounds and shot 50.2 percent from the field this season, all career highs.
When All-Star centre Alonzo Mourning when down with a foot injury in February Austin picked up his game, averaging 15.1 points and 8.2 rebounds in the 14 games he started.
He scored at least 10 points 39 times and grabbed 10 or more rebounds 13 times in helping Miami record a franchise-record 61 wins.
Before going to Turkey, Austin spent parts of three seasons with the Philadelphia 76ers and Utah Jazz.
